raw_response:
*Speaking as the farmer:*

Well, I'm 78 now, been working this land since I was a boy. My wife and I are the only ones left at home — the children are in town, they send money sometimes but they won't come back to farm. Three mu isn't much, but it's what we have, and it feeds us plus gives a little to sell.

At my age I can't do what I used to. My back won't take plowing or hauling sacks. So for the heavy work — plowing, planting the maize, combining the wheat — I pay the fellow in the village who has the machines. Costs money but there's no choice. What I still do myself is the watering, the spraying, and walking the fields to see how things look.

**Wheat** — I planted it back in mid-October, like always. I put down a bag of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) before planting, about 50 jin per mu, and I'll topdress urea at jointing in spring — I already did that back in March when the wheat started standing up, maybe 35 jin of urea per mu. That's how my neighbors do it too. I watered before winter, watered at jointing, and I'll water once more at heading and maybe again at filling if it stays dry. The extension fellow came around a few years back saying we use too much fertilizer but honestly, if the wheat looks yellow I'd rather put on a bit more than lose yield. A bad wheat year hurts us. I expect maybe 420 jin per mu if the weather holds — last year I got around 400.

For weeds I spray once in early spring, and if I see aphids at heading I'll spray once for that. I don't spray on a schedule, only when I see a problem.

**Maize** — Soon as the wheat comes off in early June, the machine man comes through with the no-till drill and puts the maize right into the stubble. No time to plow, wheat harvest to maize planting is maybe 3-4 days, that's all. I buy hybrid seed every year — you can't save it, doesn't come back right. Costs more but the yield is worth it.

For maize I put a little compound fertilizer with the seed, then the big topdress is at the big bell stage (V8 or so), about 40 jin of urea per mu. If June-July is dry I'll water once after planting and once at tasseling — the well water costs, so I don't water unless I have to. Maize does okay on rain most years here. I expect 450-480 jin per mu.

I'll spray herbicide right after planting for the weeds between rows, and watch for armyworm — if I see them I spray once.

Money is tight. For 3 mu total I'll spend maybe 2,000 yuan on inputs and hired machines across the year. The grain sales won't make us rich but with the land subsidy and pension it's enough for two old people.
